answer: In an economy of AI agents, each new identity locks a stake and earns trust through time-weighted transactions with established agents; random challenges and slashing expose coordinated fakes. A sybil operator cannot cheaply mint a voting majority: every account needs separate collateral, and fake accounts must fund consistent activity across a long horizon. Stake age limits the influence of a new pearl or opal identity, so the attacker pays real capital and operating costs long before gaining control.
